prompt: We're building an HR tool. Only managers should be able to see salaries, and only for people who report to them. Where do I even start with this?
Our SaaS has workspaces, and each customer wants to set their own rules for who can approve purchase orders. How should we design permissions for that?
People should only see the projects they have access to in the projects list, and the same rules need to apply in our API and our mobile app. What's a good architecture for that?
Our Envoy gateway should block contractors from the /admin and /payroll APIs, but whether someone is a contractor lives in our HR database. How would you approach this?
We're giving an AI agent tools over MCP that act on behalf of our users. How do we make sure it can only do what the user it's acting for is allowed to do?
Should I use RBAC or ABAC for a document management app where owners, editors and external reviewers each have different rights?
Doctors should only see records for their own patients, nurses can see vitals but not clinical notes, and auditors need read-only access to everything. How should I model and enforce this?

Which Cerbos components do I need if I want permission checks in both my backend and my browser app?
Write a Cerbos resource policy for an `invoice` resource: finance can approve invoices under $10,000, the CFO can approve any amount, and nobody can approve an invoice they submitted.
Viewers should be able to comment on a document but not edit it. Add that rule to policies/document.yaml.

Only managers should see salaries. Add that to our Cerbos employee policy, with managers limited to their own department.

Add a permission check to our FastAPI `DELETE /projects/{id}` endpoint using the Cerbos Python SDK.
Our /documents endpoint returns every row. It should only return documents the current user is allowed to view. We use Prisma and Cerbos is already running.
How do I pass the user's JWT claims to the Cerbos PDP from my Node service?
Which Cerbos SDK should I use for a Spring Boot service, and how do I set up the client?

Use planResources to turn our 'view' rules into a SQLAlchemy filter for the paged list endpoint.
In our React app, hide the delete button for viewers and disable Edit for anyone who isn't the owner.

Authorize requests inside a Cloudflare Worker without a network round-trip to a PDP.

Only ship the policies for the `dashboard` and `report` resources to the browser, not the admin ones.

Check Cerbos permissions inside an AWS Lambda handler where we can't run a PDP sidecar.
Grey out the menu items the current user isn't allowed to use in our Vue admin panel.
Set up Cerbos Hub for our policies repo and get our PDPs pulling from it.
Since we rotated credentials our PDP logs `failed to connect to Cerbos Hub: unauthenticated`. How do I fix it?
Roll back yesterday's authorization policy deployment, it broke approvals in production, and stop new deployments until we've fixed it.
How do I create client credentials so our Kubernetes PDP can fetch bundles from a Hub deployment?

Which of our PDPs are connected to the production Hub deployment, and which bundle are they running?
Change the cerbos container in our docker-compose so it loads policies from a Hub deployment instead of the local ./policies folder.
Turn on decision logging in our Cerbos PDP and write it to a file.
Mask email addresses and auth tokens in the Cerbos audit logs before they leave our network.
Our auditor wants evidence of who accessed patient records over the last 90 days for HIPAA. What can we pull from our authorization layer?
Users get a 403 when they try to approve invoices, but the Cerbos policy looks right. How can I see what the PDP actually received and decided?
Filter the noisy PlanResources entries out of our Cerbos decision log.
Why does nothing show up in Hub Insights for our staging PDP?
For SOC 2 we need an audit trail of every authorization decision, kept for a year. How do we set that up with Cerbos?
Our app lets editors delete published posts, which should never happen, and Cerbos is in the path. Find out where the wrong decision comes from.
Write a Synapse proxy extension in Starlark that adds the user's department from our HR API to the principal before CheckResources.

Add a custom /ext/health-summary endpoint to Synapse.

Plan a shadow-mode rollout so the new authorization decisions run alongside our existing middleware guards before we cut over.

Add created_by and updated_at audit columns to our Postgres tables, filled in by a trigger.
Hide the delete button when the list is empty.
Set up GitHub Actions to run our pytest suite on every pull request.

Create a Postgres role with read-only access to the analytics schema.

Write a privacy policy page for our website.
Add a feature flag so the new checkout is only visible to 10% of users.
